startup.name: Spott
startup.description: Spott is an AI native applicant tracking and CRM system for recruiting and staffing firms, with AI agents across the placement workflow. Recruiting agencies pay per seat. Team of 50 in Leuven, Belgium, Winter 2025 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Already in the batch, so this is reported for completeness only. Start from the roughly 1 percent prior for a random applicant in references/yc_acceptance.md (band 0.6 to 2 percent), then adjust: a clear buyer and a team of 50 lift it about 2x, an AI native pitch fits current YC interest, and the crowded ATS space with peer YC companies takes some back; no traction is stated.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because AI native ATS for agencies already had YC companies (Stardex, Crew) and a dominant incumbent in Bullhorn, and a European team of 50 with no stated revenue is a heavy cost base for a batch company. The acceptance estimate is a prior for a random applicant and does not rank this company, and since it is already in the batch it matters only as context for the ladder.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: seed 47% / 53% / 59%, cond 53% (n=878). Timing: months_to_seed p25 4, p50 8, p75 20 (n=468).
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor of 0.53 is the ever reached figure. The window is 22 months, which covers roughly 78 percent of B2B seed raises by timing, giving about 0.41. I keep 0.40 and do not lift for the team of 50 or the hot AI theme, per the winners test rule. A team of 50 may already be funded before YC, which could lower the need for a new round. This number does not rank Spott against other companies.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M from angels and micro funds, the YC deal alone (about $500K) is excluded by the seed definition. A 50 person team has high payroll, so a very small round is unlikely to be enough.
Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, near the 2022 and later median of $3.5M in round_benchmarks.csv, which includes the YC deal and reads low, so this band carries the most weight.
Larger institutional seed where press covered 2026 raises had a median of $6.0M (quartiles $4.3M and $10M, n=77, press leans to big rounds); needs live revenue or a standout team story.
Upside seed above $12M, seen in 2025 AI categories when several funds bid for a team with early enterprise traction.

ladder.why_it_fails: Staffing software is dominated by Bullhorn, with Loxo and others adding AI, and YC peers Stardex (S21) and Crew (S21) already sell AI native ATS and CRM to agencies, so investors will ask why Spott wins. A European base far from US staffing buyers makes distribution hard. A team of 50 suggests earlier funding or revenue, so a new priced round above $1M is not certain to be needed or announced in the window.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_a cond 26% (n=468), ever 14% known-only, range 12% to 25%. Timing: months_to_series_a p25 21, median 28, p75 37 (n=123).
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the ever reached figure. The window is 22 months and the p25 of months to Series A is 21, so only about a third to half of eventual Series A raisers get there in time, and 0.26 times that gives roughly 0.11.

bands.rationale: Thin or small Series A, common for vertical software with early but modest revenue. A larger team with existing agency customers can reach a Series A sooner than a founder pair.
Central band around the 2022 and later Series A median of $15M (p25 $11M, p75 $21M).
Strong growth round led by a top tier fund.
Upside where the category is hot and revenue compounds fast.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs predictable annual recurring revenue from recruiting agencies, who are slow to switch away from Bullhorn and often use a handful of seats. Stardex (S21) and Crew (S21) sold the same product pitch for years, and Lever (S12), the YC ATS winner, needed several years to reach scale. Inside the window Spott would need about $1M to $2M of recurring revenue after seed.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_b cond 21% (n=123), ever 3% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the ever reached rate given Series A. A Series B inside a window of 22 months is rare because months_to_series_b has a median of 32 to 47 months from the batch start in time_to_milestones.csv, so only a breakout gets there.

bands.rationale: Thin Series B or bridge round of $10M to $20M, typical when growth is real but slower than the Series A story promised and investors want to see more revenue.
Central band; the 2022 and later Series B median is $40M.
Hot company band; the 2022 and later post money median is $600M.
Breakout upside above $70M at a valuation near $1B, reached only by the few companies that compound revenue quickly after a Series A.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B inside the window would need revenue near $10M from agencies, which almost no company of this kind does in under two years. Lever (S12) took years from batch to a Series B in the researched data, and Stardex (S21) shows the same slow path, so the window is too short for this step unless the company breaks out early.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --industry B2B: series_c cond 19% (n=26), ever 1% known-only.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is conditional on Series B and ever reached, from a tiny sample. Inside the window almost nobody reaches Series C, so I keep a low nonzero figure for a breakout path with several fast rounds.

bands.rationale: Thin extension or flat round of $20M to $40M, used when a company needs more runway before it proves a Series C story.
Central band; the 2022 and later Series C median is $74M.
Strong growth round of $80M to $150M led by a growth fund, tied to a clear revenue ramp and category leadership.
Category leader upside above $150M at a multibillion valuation, seen only for the few companies that win a large market outright.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C inside the window is close to impossible for a recruiting software company still in its second year, which would need several consecutive hypergrowth rounds. The researched Series C companies such as Lever (S12) took roughly four to five years from batch, and nothing visible today points to the category defining ramp that would be required.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely Spott stalls or is bought small: Bullhorn, Loxo and other incumbents add AI agents to their ATS, agency customers churn as the staffing cycle weakens, and the company sells to a larger HR platform. Stardex and Crew are YC S21 peers in the same wedge with no later round found in the data, and Lever sold to Employ after reaching scale.

analogs.relevance: Summer 2021 AI native ATS and CRM for executive search
analogs.outcome_summary: Active in the same wedge; shows the product exists and the agency market is slow to convert.

analogs.relevance: Summer 2021 ATS and CRM for recruiting agencies
analogs.outcome_summary: Active with an agency ATS; no breakout round found in the data.
Grew into a large ATS and was acquired; the upside path, but for an in house recruiting buyer.

analogs.relevance: Winter 2020 recruiting software for data driven teams
analogs.outcome_summary: Active small company; shows slow outcomes in recruiting tech.

killers.risk: Bullhorn and other incumbents add AI to their base
killers.evidence: Bullhorn dominates agency ATS with more than ten thousand agencies and sells AI as an embedded layer; Loxo is an all in one rival.
killers.mitigation: Win a niche such as executive search or high volume staffing with a measurable placement lift.

killers.risk: Agency churn and a weak hiring cycle
killers.evidence: Staffing demand is cyclical and small agencies cut software first.
killers.mitigation: Move upmarket to mid size staffing firms and price on placements.

killers.risk: Europe based team selling to US buyers
killers.evidence: Distribution into US staffing firms needs local sales and references.
killers.mitigation: Open a US sales presence and use agency partners.

competition_now.name: Bullhorn
competition_now.what: Dominant applicant tracking and CRM for staffing and recruiting agencies with AI layered in

competition_now.name: Loxo
competition_now.what: All in one ATS, CRM and sourcing tool
competition_now.traction: Named among leading AI recruiting tools

competition_now.name: Spreadsheets and legacy ATS (status quo)
competition_now.what: Manual data entry and fragmented add ons

technical_complexity.rationale: A full ATS and CRM is a large build, but AI agents on top of it are simple to prototype; the hard parts are data migration from Bullhorn, email and calendar sync, and trusted candidate matching. With 50 people the team can ship a lot, but still faces integration breadth.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents have the data and the customers and are already shipping AI features, so a copy is a year or less of work for them.

evidence.claim: Staffing industry analysts argued in December 2024 that firms risk falling behind without integrated AI tools
Vendors describe AI as a core layer on the ATS and CRM for agencies, with adoption rising, per vendor sources

roadmap.goal: Show agencies switch from their ATS and place more candidates
actions: Track placements per recruiter before and after
roadmap.proof: Documented placement lift and paid seats

roadmap.goal: Scale into mid size staffing firms and a US go to market
actions: Hire a US head of sales
Launch an AI agent add on priced per placement
roadmap.proof: $2M annual recurring revenue with low churn

pros.evidence: Team of 50 at batch start suggests real product and some revenue, rare for Winter 2025.

pros.point: AI adoption among staffing firms is rising
pros.evidence: Vendor sources report adoption growing as agencies look for AI native tools.

brand.name: Spott
weaknesses: Double t looks like a typo of Spot, which is widely used
brand.rationale: A very short name that hints at spotting talent, but the spelling clashes with Spot, a common brand. YC recruiting cases such as Lever (S12) show a plain short name can anchor a large ATS company, so the name is neutral.

narrative.headline: A big team in a crowded agency software space; a priced seed inside 22 months is a little under even odds.
narrative.general_summary: Spott sells an AI native ATS and CRM to recruiting agencies. The team is unusually large and AI adoption among agencies is rising, but Bullhorn dominates and YC peers Stardex and Crew already sell the same pitch. Inside a 22 month window the seed probability follows the B2B timing curve, not a lift for team size. A large existing team may also reduce the need for an announced round. A Series A inside the window is unlikely. The odds do not rank Spott against other companies. The forecast window runs from the as of date to 2026-11-17, and later rounds are only counted if they close inside it.

assumptions: Only the input file was used about the company; no site, directory page or news about it was read.
Seed means a round above about $1M from outside investors, not the standard YC deal of about $500K, that closes inside the window.
The company is already in YC, so the acceptance figure is reported for completeness only.
Web search covered the market only. Results dated after the as of date or naming the company were to be ignored; none named it.
Funding coverage in the repo data is incomplete (see base_rates.py ranges), so the anchors are lower to upper ranges and not exact.
